key_insight: Adding Tikhonov regularization to PINNs resolves the non-uniqueness of terminal-state distributed control for parabolic PDEs by steering the learned solution toward a stable minimum-energy control.
engineering_relevance: This makes PINN-based PDE control more reliable for applications that need smooth, physically meaningful actuation with low control energy.
method: Formulate terminal-state tracking control for parabolic PDEs with a Tikhonov penalty on the distributed control.
Train a PINN to minimize the regularized objective using PDE residuals, terminal-state mismatch, and quadrature-based approximations.
Prove consistency and derive an error bound linking control accuracy to training residuals and the regularization parameter.
evidence_signal: Experiments on the linear heat equation and nonlinear Burgers' equation show accurate terminal-state matching with lower-energy, smoother controls than unregularized baselines.
watch_item: Performance depends on careful tuning of the regularization weight and on residual/quadrature accuracy, since overly weak or strong regularization can bias the control solution.
paper_title: Tikhonov-Regularized Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Terminal-State Distributed Optimal Control of Parabolic Partial Differential Equations
